newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Wait and see attitude on new wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Wait and see attitude on new wheat crop.

text.p: A wait and see attitude prevailed on Australia's 1997/98 wheat crop prospects despite the Australian Bureau of Meteorology's report of a continued El Nino effect, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday.

Fears concerning the El Nino report, which suggested Australia faced a dry winter and spring, were moderated by good subsoil moisture in much of Australia's wheat regions, the AWB said in its weekly grain market report.
Understanding remained limited of how the new crop would be affected, it said.

"In the coming months the industry will be watching rainfall levels very closely as June rainbands moving across the continent will continue to provide potential to improve ground moisture in the drier southern areas," it said.
Falling Chicago prices caused by positive wheat planting and winter crop reports also provided some downward pressure in Sydney, it said.
Some demand for feed grains continued in wheat and triticale, but sorghum prices eased as stock feed were now largely covered in southern Queensland and northern New South Wales (NSW), it said.
The sorghum harvest is 90 percent complete in NSW and 50 percent complete in Queensland.
The harvest should begin to move into Victoria and to affect prices in that state in coming weeks, it said.
